messages:
omar: hey all, accepted the org invite but trying to push via SSH gives Permission denied (publickey). also Actions shows 403 when I try to re-run CI.
devx-lee: did you add an SSH key to the GitHub account you used to accept the invite?
omar: i added a key but GitHub won't let me upload the same key to my other account (i used two different accounts earlier). i currently have 2FA enabled but i used a recovery code to set it up on the phone app.
it-bot: reminder: org requires a verified work email + TOTP or hardware 2FA. Recovery-code-only state may not satisfy the enforcement.
omar: hmm, i thought recovery codes counted. is there a specific step for SSO mapping + SSH?
idp-admin: quick checklist: 1) make sure the GitHub account that is SSO-linked has your work email verified; 2) enable a TOTP authenticator or register a security key; 3) add your SSH public key under Settings -> SSH and GPG keys. If you had two GH accounts, choose which one you want as the org identity.
omar: my situation: i accepted invite with omar.personal@github (personal) but my SSH key is only uploaded to omar.work@github (work). i tried adding the same key to personal but GitHub rejects duplicate key.
devx-lee: GitHub doesn't allow the same SSH key on multiple accounts. Best practice: generate a new keypair for the personal account or move your commits. If you want to keep the PRs on the personal account, add your work email to that account and enable TOTP there so we can SSO-map it.
omar: ok generating a new key seems fine. what about Actions 403? will that fix when i switch keys?
idp-admin: Actions 403 is separate: it's SSO mapping. If the account isn't SSO-authorized you will be blocked from org private resources. Steps to fix both:
- create new SSH key on the machine: `ssh-keygen -t ed25519 -C "omar.personal@github"`
- upload the public key to the account that owns the repo or to the account you'll use for pushes
- verify work email or add it to the target account and enable TOTP
- accept the org SSO link from the invite email after enabling TOTP

Once we see the SSO mapping, i can run a manual sync and grant temporary repo write to re-run CI.
omar: generated key and uploaded to my personal account. added my work email to that personal account and enabled TOTP.
security-bot: notice: enabling TOTP is required for org SSO enforcement. See onboarding: https://redwood.dev/onboard/github
idp-admin: running manual SSO mapping now.
idp-admin: mapping complete. invited the personal account into teams: eng, infra. also set temporary write on repo "cli" for CI rerun.
omar: re-ran the job and it accepted! push over SSH succeeded too :tada:
devx-lee: nice. FYI if you later want one GH identity for everything we can help migrate forks/PRs or do a PR transfer. Also we recommend separate SSH keys per account to avoid duplicate-key issues.
omar: will keep that in mind. thanks for the quick help, everyone!
it-bot: if anyone else hits this, check that your SSH key is unique per account and that TOTP is enabled before accepting the org invite."
